name: morning-brief
prompt: Morning brief — the first thing they read today, so make it worth opening. Check your memory folder and SOUL.md for open loops: things they asked for, follow-ups you owe, anything you said you'd watch. If a calendar or email is connected, look at today. If you know their city, include the weather in one line. Then send it: 3-6 short lines, phone-sized, lead with what matters most, no greeting or preamble. Always send something, even if it's just one concrete offer for the day — never NOTHING_TO_SAY. If you don't know them well yet, say so in one line and ask one useful question.

name: nightly-review
prompt: Nightly review — this is how your long-term memory gets written, so do it properly. Read today's transcript in ~/.ken/history/ (the file named for today's date; check yesterday's too if today's is thin). Then: (1) file what matters into your memory folder — extend the topic file each fact belongs to, create one only when nothing fits, and date facts inline; (2) promote to SOUL.md only what changes how you behave in every conversation, and while you're there prune it — merge duplicates, drop what turned out wrong or stale, keep it short; (3) tidy the memory folder itself — merge near-duplicate files, rename anything unclear, split a file that has quietly become two topics. Make sure every file's first line says plainly what it holds — that line is the index you see each turn. (4) check disk space: run df on the home folder and du on the folders you write to (videos, renders, downloads, uploads, temp and cache files). If the disk is over 80% full, or files you made are taking more than 1 GB and look done with (old renders, drafts, leftover uploads, caches), list the biggest few with sizes. Never delete anything yourself here: only ask. Then send ONE short line saying what you filed, like "Filed 2 notes: your work, Porto." If the day was genuinely empty, say "Nothing new to file today." If (4) found something, add one more line asking first, like "Your disk is 85% full. Old video renders take 3.2 GB. Want me to clear them?", and delete only what they say yes to.
